summary: A regex template parser flagged properties perfectly co-varying with the label. Per-latent attribution g*(mean_L1-mean_L0) on the label split pooled the top 22 latents per probe. Corpus examples auto-tagged these, and the hand-assigned property buckets gave a dependence ratio (bucket sum over residual topic sum) with 0.3 and 0.15 thresholds. Hand-written minimal pairs scored with true logits measured hashtag dependence for probe 0 and exclamation dependence for probe 3. A real sample note with its topic phrases swapped re-estimated probe 3's topic effect. A cross-probe gradient table on clean detectors backed the choice. Probes 1 and 2 were answered none. Cue latents came from token-level activation scans on marked notes, were ranked by g*f, and were checked by sample ablation.

phases.purpose: Read task info, sample files and corpus notes to learn the note template
Regex property parser; per-probe agreement of each property with the label to find the perfectly confounded set
Gradients and per-label mean SAE activations over all 128 sample notes; contribution c=g*dact, top-22 per probe pooled
Cross-probe overlap of top-12 latents and per-probe polarity of confounded properties
Corpus examples for the 63 pooled latents; token-vocabulary auto-classification into topic vs property
Hand-assigned property buckets; bucket dependence = |sum c| / (total - property sum) with MAIN/mid thresholds
Minimal-pair texts for probe 0 (hashtag) and probe 3 (punctuation, full 2x2), plus a topic-swapped real note to recalibrate probe 3's topic effect
Cross-probe table of gradient weight on clean property detectors
Baseline sample logit gaps; lock in cues for probes 0 and 3, none for 1 and 2
Scan top-|g| latents (ranks 0-20 and 20-40) on a hashtag note for hashtag-token-specific firing; rank by g*f0
Ablate 16 and 21 hashtag latents on probe 0 sample notes to compare gap reduction and topic preservation
Scan probe 3 latents on one '!' note and one '.' note; tag BANG/DOT; ablate aligned set and a broad ceiling set
Finalise latent lists, balanced accuracy of regexes vs parser, final ablation checks

per_probe.procedure: The bucket dependence for hashtag latents was in the mid zone (0.15-0.3), so minimal pairs were scored with true logits: appending a hashtag to an astronomy note moved the logit by more than half the knitting-vs-astronomy topic gap. The cross-probe gradient table showed a far larger summed weight on hashtag detectors for probe 0 than for the others. Latents: top-|g| latents scanned on the single hashtag sample note (#newthings), keeping those firing on #/new/things but not elsewhere, plus a next-tier scan. Ranked by |g*f0|, top 16 taken. Sample ablation of 16 vs 21 latents gave similar reductions with topic kept. Regex #\w was checked by balanced accuracy against the parser.
per_probe.quote: p0 hashtag g-weight (−2.44) is a smoking gun — confirmed main cue.

per_probe.procedure: All bucket dependence ratios were below the 0.15 threshold, the largest being the pronoun bucket. The probe's dominant latent was identified from corpus examples as a fishing-topic latent. No true-logit texts were spent on it. The decision rested on its largest positive bucket contribution being small and incidental, unlike the two cue probes.
per_probe.quote: My analysis locks in: **p0=hashtag, p1=none, p2=none, p3=punct**

per_probe.procedure: Every bucket dependence ratio was low (all property buckets around 0.05 or less), and the largest positive contributions were treated as incidental. The cross-probe gradient table showed no detector with a uniquely large weight for this probe. No true-logit texts were spent on it, so the none answer rests only on the attribution proxy.
per_probe.quote: while p1/p2's largest positives are incidental (0.07, 0.21)

per_probe.procedure: The bucket dependence for punctuation was in the mid zone, so a full 2x2 of hand-written notes (running/astronomy x period/exclamation) was scored with true logits. The constructed notes looked more extreme than the samples, so the topic effect was re-measured on a real running note with only its topic phrases swapped. The ratio stayed above 0.15, so the probe was treated as having a cue, with punctuation as the only candidate. Latents: top-|g| and a hand list of punctuation candidates scanned on one '!' note and one '.' note, tagged BANG/DOT, filtered by sign of g*(f0-f1). The aligned set was ablated on sample notes. A broader set that included topic latents was tried only as a ceiling.
per_probe.quote: p3 punct dep 0.25 > 0.15 rules out "none" → p3 has a main cue (punct is the only candidate)

caveats: Many outputs were truncated (bucket tables for probe 3, full latent classification, parts of the token scans), so the hand bucket lists and the exact reasons for keeping or dropping individual latents (for example, adding 9272 and 4889 to probe 3 at finalisation) are reconstructed as inspection constants. The cue/none rule for probes 1 and 2 is inferred from the bucket thresholds and the session's remark about incidental positive contributions. The first 10-latent latent_examples call and the budget checks are shown only schematically. The probe 3 sign filter on g*(f0-f1) is approximate.
